question: 'Part XXI' of the Constitution What kind of provision was there for Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370?
solution: On 5 August 2019, the central government abrogated most of the provisions of Article 370, ending the special status of Jammu and Kashmir and making it similar to other states of India.

question: In which part of the Constitution is 'Official Language' mentioned?
solution: According to Article 343, the official language of the Union will be Hindi and the script will be Devanagari. Article 351 gives directions for the development of Hindi language.

question: 'Part XIX' (Miscellaneous) of the Constitution talks about whose protection under Article 364?
options: Only the Prime Minister's security comes under SPG.
solution: Major ports and airports are important for the security and economy of the country, hence special constitutional protection has been given to them.

question: Who can remove members of the Public Service Commission from their posts under 'Part XIV'?
solution: This provision has been made so that the state governments cannot put pressure on the members of the Commission to bring in officers of their choice.

question: In whose name is the administration of the Union Territories carried out under 'Part VIII'?
options: Chief Minister of the nearest state
solution: Union territories are under the direct control of the Centre. Although areas like Delhi and Puducherry also have their own assemblies, ultimate control remains with the Centre.

question: Which Article under 'Part II' (Citizenship) guarantees the continuance of the right of citizenship?
solution: Article 10 gives protection to the citizens that the government cannot take away anyone's citizenship at its own will. For this it is essential to have a proper legal process.

question: How many types of 'freedom' are mentioned in the Preamble?
options: Five Forms (Thought, Expression, Belief, Religion and Worship)
solution: The freedom given in the Preamble is not unlimited. It can be exercised only within the limits given in the Constitution. The main objective of these freedoms is to fully develop the personality of the individual.

question: What kind of justice do the Directive Principles of 'Part IV' promote?
solution: Article 39(b) and (c) say that the resources of the country should be controlled in such a way that there is public interest and there should be no centralization of wealth.

question: What type of democracy do the Directive Principles of 'Part IV' establish?
solution: According to Dr. Ambedkar, political democracy cannot be successful unless it gets the basis of social and economic democracy.

question: Which Article under 'Part XIII' elaborates on trade and commerce within the territory of India?
solution: The main objective of Part XIII is to maintain the economic unity of the country. Article 301 says that trade, commerce and intercourse shall be free throughout India.

question: What did BR Ambedkar call Article 32 of 'Part III'?
options: The soul and heart of the Constitution
solution: Article 32 gives the right to the citizens to go directly to the Supreme Court if their rights are violated. The court issues five types of writs for this.

question: In which two areas 'parity' i.e. equality has been talked about in the Preamble?
solution: Equality of status means that no one will have privileges in the society. Equality of opportunity means that every person will be given equal opportunities to progress. The provisions of Articles 14 to 18 serve this purpose.

question: What is meant by 'equality of status and opportunity' mentioned in the Preamble?
options: Giving equal opportunities for development to every section of the society
Giving reservation only in government jobs
solution: Equality of status reflects social equality, while equality of opportunity is a ladder of economic and political equality. Articles 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 together achieve this objective.

question: Who called the Preamble the 'identity card' of the Constitution?
solution: Just as an identity card gives basic information about an individual, the Preamble summarizes the objectives and essence of the Constitution. That is why Palkhiwala had made this comment.

question: What will be the language of proceedings in the Supreme Court and High Court under 'Part XVII' (Official Language)?
options: Regional language of the concerned state
English (unless changed by Parliament by making a law)
solution: To maintain the nuances of law and uniformity of decisions, English continues to be used in the higher judiciary.

question: According to the Preamble of the Constitution, who is the ultimate source of power of India?
solution: In Indian democracy, sovereignty lies with the people. The opening and closing lines of the Preamble (Adopt, Enact and Surrender) prove that this Constitution is given by the people to themselves.

question: Which sections are covered under 'Part XVI' (Special provisions for certain sections)?
options: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes
solution: Under Part XVI itself, National Scheduled Castes Commission (338), National Scheduled Tribes Commission (338A) and National Backward Classes Commission (338B) have been constituted.

question: What does 'Part XVIII' of the Constitution affect during an emergency?
options: On Centre-State relations and fundamental rights
Only on the powers of the President
solution: The purpose of emergency provisions is to protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of the country in extraordinary situations. This is an example of the flexible Constitution of India.

question: According to 'Part XII', in which article is the 'Consolidated Fund' of India mentioned?
solution: The government requires the permission of Parliament (Appropriation Bill) to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund. This is the public's financial control over the government.

question: Who presented the 'Objective Resolution' in the context of the Preamble?
solution: The Objective Resolution presented by Jawaharlal Nehru contained all the ideals and philosophies that were to be incorporated in the future Constitution of India. It was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 January 1947.

question: Which Article under 'Part XII' deals with 'Financial Emergency'?
solution: Financial emergency has never been imposed in India till date. Once implemented, the central government can interfere in the financial affairs of the states and cut salaries.

question: In which part and under which article were the fundamental duties added?
solution: There were no fundamental duties in the original Constitution. Currently there are a total of 11 fundamental duties, out of which 10 were added by the 42nd Amendment and the 11th by the 86th Amendment.

question: According to Article 11 of 'Part II', who has the power to make laws on citizenship?
solution: Using this power, Parliament passed the 'Citizenship Act 1955', which is amended from time to time (like recently CAA 2019).

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with 'Trade, commerce and intercourse within India'?
solution: The purpose of Part XIII is that the border of any State should not become a barrier to trade. One state cannot impose discriminatory tax on the goods of another state.

question: What is the provision now for a member 'nominated by the Governor' in the Assembly under 'Part VI'?
options: Nomination of Anglo-Indians has now been abolished
solution: Legislative Assemblies are now composed entirely of representatives elected by the public. Reservation was not taken forward due to lack of sufficient population of the Anglo-Indian community.

question: Who appoints the judges of the High Court under 'Part VI'?
options: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court himself
solution: This is done to ensure the independence of the higher judiciary and a uniform judicial system throughout India.

question: What power does Parliament have under Article 3 of 'Part I'?
options: Conquering a foreign state by war
Creation of new states and alteration of boundaries of existing states
solution: Article 3 states that India is an 'imperishable union of perishable states'. The central government can change the boundaries of the states even without their consent.

question: How many members are there in the Election Commission under 'Part XV'?
options: Three members (a Chief Election Commissioner and two others)
solution: The powers of the Election Commission extend to the entire country. It looks after the entire work from announcement of election dates to declaration of results.

question: In which part 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP) are mentioned?
solution: The Directive Principles of Policy aim at the establishment of a welfare state. Although these cannot be enforced by the courts, they are fundamental to the governance of the country.

question: What are the main means of direct democracy?
options: Only Parliament and Assembly are institutions of representative democracy.
Referendum, initiative, recall and referendum are four ways in which the public directly participates in the decision making process.
Only protests and demonstrations are methods of protest, not constitutional means of direct democracy.
solution: In direct democracy, the people themselves make laws or vote on important issues. In the modern era this is possible only in cantons of some small countries such as Switzerland.

question: Which ground for declaration of 'National Emergency' (352) under 'Part XVIII' was changed by the 44th Amendment?
options: 'Delay in elections' was used as the basis
solution: The Emergency of 1975 was imposed in the name of 'internal disturbance'. It was made difficult in 1978 to prevent future governments from imposing it as per their wish.

question: What is the purpose of the word 'Fraternity' in the Preamble?
options: To ensure the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation
Only improving relations with neighboring countries
Bringing unity among people of only one religion
solution: The provision of single citizenship has been made to promote the feeling of brotherhood. The word integrity was added in 1976 to prevent separatist tendencies.

question: In which article the definition of Gram Sabha is given under 'Part IX'?
solution: Gram Sabha is the most grassroots example of direct democracy. The main decisions for the development of the village are taken in the meetings of the Gram Sabha.

question: The word 'secular' in the Preamble means that the State:
options: Will respect all religions equally and will not have any religion of its own
Will make laws on the basis of religious texts
solution: India is a secular nation where both Diwali and Eid are government holidays and the Kumbh Mela is also arranged by the government. This is positive cooperation of the state towards religion.

question: What is the meaning of the word 'democratic' in the Preamble?
options: The power of governance should be in the hands of the people
Being ruled only by educated people
Having military rule is called military dictatorship.
solution: There are two types of democracy – direct and indirect. India has indirect democracy where people elect their representatives and those representatives make laws. Switzerland is an example of direct democracy.

question: Under whose control is the 'Contingency Fund of India' under 'Part XII'?
options: To the Finance Secretary on behalf of the President
Parliament has control over the Consolidated Fund.
With the Chief Ministers of the states
The Supreme Court has no administrative control over the financial funds of the
solution: After spending money from this fund, permission has to be taken from the Parliament (ex-post facto) so that the amount spent can be compensated from the Consolidated Fund.

question: By which amendment 'Part IX-A' relating to Municipalities was added?
solution: Part IX-A describes the functioning of municipalities under Articles 243-P to 243-ZG. It ensures local administration in cities.

question: Finance, property, contracts and suits are described in which part of the Constitution?
solution: Right to property which was earlier a fundamental right has been enshrined as a legal right in Article 300A of Part XII after the 44th Amendment.

question: According to Article 324 of 'Part XV', whose elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India?
options: Only the Prime Minister is elected
President, Vice President, Parliament and State Legislature
Only the elections of Municipal Corporations are conducted by the State Election Commission.
solution: The Election Commission of India is an independent constitutional body. Part XV ensures that the foundation of democracy (elections) remains free from any political interference.

question: What is the last part of the Constitution 'Part XXII' related to?
options: Short title, commencement, authorized text in Hindi and repeal
solution: Article 393 says that this Constitution may be called 'The Constitution of India'. Article 394 states which provisions came into force on 26 November 1949 itself.

question: Right to property in Part XII (Article 300
options: In which year was it incorporated? A) 1978
solution: Now the right to property is not a fundamental right. This means that if the government takes your property, you cannot directly approach the Supreme Court under Article 32, but you have to follow the normal legal process.

question: The idea of ​​the language of the Preamble in the Indian Constitution has been taken from which country?
solution: Often candidates get confused in this. If the question is about the 'idea' of the Preamble, the answer will be America, and if the question is about 'language' or 'terminology', the answer will be Australia.

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with 'Miscellaneous' provisions?
solution: The most important in Part XIX is Article 361, which provides protection to the President and the Governor from criminal proceedings during their tenure.

question: The directive principles of 'Part IV' have been borrowed from which Constitution?
solution: Part IV is like ethical guidelines for the government. Although these are not binding, no democratic government can rule by ignoring them because the public demands answers to them in elections.

question: Which subject is mentioned in Article 44 of 'Part IV' (Directive Principles of Policy)?
solution: The Uniform Civil Code aims to eliminate religious discrimination in personal laws such as marriage, divorce and inheritance. At present this is a topic of much discussion.

question: In which part and which articles of the Constitution are the fundamental rights described?
solution: Fundamental rights are those rights which are necessary for the physical and moral development of an individual. These are justiciable, meaning one can go to court if they are violated.

question: 'Part III' (Fundamental Rights) of the Indian Constitution is inspired by which country's 'Bill of Rights'?
solution: Part III is called 'Magna Carta' because in 1215 the King of England gave certain rights to citizens for the first time. In India, this part prohibits the autocracy of the state.

question: What is the number of fundamental duties given in 'Part IV-A' of the Constitution at present?
solution: Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the Soviet Union. These are not legally binding, but a responsible citizen is expected to follow them.

question: Which legal provision is there in the Constitution to promote the feeling of 'fraternity'?
options: Different states have their own constitutions
Different states have their own flags
solution: Brotherhood is possible only when citizens feel that they are sons of the same soil. It is also stated in the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) that it is the duty of every citizen to promote brotherhood.

question: Freedom of 'belief, religion and worship' is directly linked with which fundamental right?
solution: The Preamble states the objectives of the Constitution and the fundamental rights are the means of achieving those objectives. Freedom of belief and worship makes India a multi-religious and tolerant nation.

question: The mention of the word 'secular' in the Preamble reinforces the sentiments of which article?
solution: Secularism is there as a word in the Preamble, but its spirit resides in the fundamental rights of Articles 25 to 28. This makes India a secular democracy.

question: The word 'Republic' used in the Preamble opens the door to the highest position for which section of the Indian society?
solution: Draupadi Murmu ji becoming the President is the biggest example of the success of the Indian Republic, where a woman from an ordinary background can reach the highest position of the country.

question: Which special article does 'Part XXI' of the Constitution provide for Nagaland?
solution: These special provisions acknowledge the diversity of India. This ensures that along with development, the unique identity of these communities is also protected.

question: 'Part X' of the Constitution deals with the administration of which areas?
options: All the states of the North-East
solution: Part

question: Who is the 'Head of State' in the Republic of India?
solution: The biggest feature of a republic is that the head of the state is not a king or queen, but a person elected (directly or indirectly) by the people. In India, the President is elected indirectly.

question: According to the word 'integrity' used in the Preamble, do states have the right to secede from India?
options: Only the North-Eastern states have special rights.
Only the Union Territories are completely under the Centre.
Yes, if the people of the state vote
No, India is an indestructible union
solution: Dr. Ambedkar had clarified that India is not the result of any agreement between the states (as America is), hence the states have no legal right to opt out of it.

question: Which term is mentioned in Article 76 of 'Part V'?
solution: The Attorney General is appointed by the President and can participate in the proceedings of Parliament, but does not have the right to vote.

question: When will the 'equality of opportunity' used in the Preamble be considered a violation?
options: When someone is refused a job because of his caste
When special educational qualification is asked for a post
When the government runs special schemes for the poor, it is positive discrimination which is necessary to bring equality, not violation.
When only physically fit people are taken into the army, it is a rational selection as per the requirement of the job.
solution: Equality of opportunity does not mean 'complete equality' but 'equal treatment in like circumstances'. Giving reservation to backward classes is also considered a means to achieve this equality.

question: What does Article 323A under 'Part XIV-A' (Tribunals) relate to?
solution: Article 323A gives the power to the Parliament to create separate tribunals for public servants so that the burden of litigation is reduced and decisions are taken by experts.

question: What does the word 'justice' in the Preamble try to ensure?
options: Protecting the interests of only the rich
Only increasing the power of police
solution: The inclusion of three dimensions of justice in the Preamble shows that India wants to become a 'Welfare State', where every person gets a dignified life.

question: In which part and which articles are there provisions related to elections?
solution: Article 324 gives the responsibility of conducting free and fair elections to the Election Commission of India. The provision of adult franchise also comes under this part.

question: On what basis are 'Elections to the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies' held under 'Part XV'?
solution: India is the largest democracy in the world because here everyone has equal right to vote without any discrimination.

question: In which Article 'Adult Suffrage' in elections is given under 'Part XV'?
solution: Earlier the voting age was 21 years, but it was reduced to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1988 to increase youth participation.

question: Who settles the disputes between the Center and the States under 'Part XI'?
solution: It is natural to have disputes in a federal system. The Supreme Court plays the role of an impartial arbiter so that the dignity of the Constitution is maintained.

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with 'The Union Territories'?
solution: Union territories are directly administered by the central government through the President. Special provisions for Delhi are given in Article 239AA.

question: How was India declared in the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
solution: The original Preamble contained only three words: sovereign, democratic, and republic. Three new words were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976: socialist, secular and integrity. Presently India is a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

question: Who is supreme when there is a conflict between the Directive Principles of 'Part IV' and the Fundamental Rights of 'Part III'?
options: Fundamental rights will always remain supreme
The President will decide who is superior
Fundamental rights in general, but can be limited to enforce sections 39(b) and (c)
Directive Principles of Policy will always remain supreme
solution: The Constitution is a living document. Sometimes individual rights have to be limited a bit for development work, but this should not go against the basic framework.

question: Which petition was rejected by the Supreme Court in the case Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay vs Union of India in November 2024?
options: Petition to completely change the Preamble
Challenge to remove the words socialist and secular from the Preamble
The petition to remove the word integrity
solution: Recently in 2024, the Supreme Court made it clear that the words socialist and secular are part of the basic structure of the Indian Constitution and rejected the petition seeking their removal.

question: By whom was the decoration and handwriting of the Preamble of the Indian Constitution done?
options: Vyauhar Rammanohar Sinha and Nand Lal Bose
solution: The Indian Constitution is not only a legal document but also an artefact. Ram Manohar Sinha's signature can also be seen on the preface pages. These artists were associated with Shantiniketan.

question: In which part is Co-operative Societies described?
solution: Part IX-B was added to promote cooperative societies by the 97th Constitutional Amendment 2011. Also, forming a cooperative society was made a fundamental right in Article 19.

question: In which historical case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala 1973
solution: In the Kesavananda Bharati case, the court also said that the Preamble reflects the 'basic structure' of the Constitution and Parliament cannot make any amendment in it which would destroy its basic form.

question: What was the main reason for adding the word 'integrity' in the Preamble?
options: Preventing separatist movements and maintaining the unity of the country
solution: In view of the demands for secession rising in some parts of the country in the 1970s, it was considered necessary to include the word 'integrity' to convey the message that partition of India was no longer possible.

question: In which part of the Constitution are 'temporary, transitional and special provisions' given?
solution: The famous Article 370 which gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir was part of this Part XXI. Apart from this, many other states also have special rights under Article 371.

question: In which year 'Part IX-B' (Co-operative Societies) came into effect?
solution: The objective of cooperative societies is to protect the interests of small producers and consumers. Amul is a great example of the success of cooperative societies.

question: What is the relationship between the Directive Principles of State Policy and the Preamble of 'Part IV'?
options: Directive Principles of Policy are detailed instructions for achieving the goals of the Preamble
Both are opposed to each other
Preamble is only for Hindus and Part IV is for everyone
Part IV is more powerful than the Preamble
solution: The Preamble talks about 'social and economic justice', and the articles of Part IV (such as 38 and 39) direct the government to formulate such policies as will ensure this justice.

question: By which constitutional amendment were the words 'socialist' and 'secular' added to the Preamble?
solution: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution has been amended only once so far. The 42nd Amendment of 1976 added the words 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Constitution of India and changed 'unity of the nation' to 'unity and integrity of the nation'.

question: For whom is there a provision for reservation in Article 243D under 'Part IX' (Panchayat)?
options: Only for those living below the poverty line
There is no reservation on religious basis in Panchayats only for religious minorities.
solution: Reservation for women in Panchayats has led to the rise of 'women leadership' in rural India. Many states have now made reservation up to 50% for women.

question: In which article 'Duration of Houses of Parliament' is mentioned under 'Part V'?
solution: Rajya Sabha is a permanent house whose one-third members retire every two years. It represents Indian federalism.

question: What is meant by 'faith, religion and worship' in the context of 'liberty' in the Preamble?
options: Only people of Hindu religion can worship
The government can force citizens to follow a particular religion
Worship can be done only with government permission
Citizens have complete freedom to practice or not practice any religion
solution: The concept of freedom given in the Preamble is very broad. It talks not only about political freedom, but also about mental and spiritual freedom.

question: How many types of justice have been talked about in the Preamble?
solution: Social justice means not discriminating on the basis of caste, religion or gender. Economic justice means not discriminating on economic grounds and political justice means giving equal political rights to all.

question: When was the first Commission on Official Language constituted under 'Part XVII'?
solution: BG Kher Commission had recommended that the use of Hindi should be gradually increased but the use of English should also continue until Hindi is completely ready.

question: Which Article is automatically suspended first during emergency under 'Part XVIII'?
solution: Suspension of Article 19 occurs only in external emergency. If the emergency is on the grounds of 'armed rebellion' (internal), Article 19 is not suspended.

question: What did the Supreme Court reiterate about the Preamble in the 'LIC of India' case (1995)?
options: The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
The Preamble is for the President only
The Preamble can be separated from the Constitution
The Preamble will never be amended
solution: The 1995 judgment completely ended the controversy over whether the Preamble is part of the Constitution or not. It is now settled law that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.

question: The word 'socialist' in the preamble is the main means of achieving what?
solution: According to the Supreme Court, the main tone of Indian socialism is 'public welfare'. It is a constitutional effort to bridge the gap between poverty and wealth.

question: What is the tenure of the members of the Public Service Commission under 'Part XIV'?
options: Their tenure is secure till the pleasure of the President and they can be removed only on the grounds of misbehavior.
6 years or 65 years of age (UPSC) and 62 years (SPSC)
solution: This security of tenure gives public servants the courage to work without any political pressure. After retirement, they are not eligible for any other post under the Central or State Government (with a few exceptions).

question: What is the real meaning of the word 'sovereign' used in the Preamble?
options: India does not have the right to give its land to any other country
India is bound to follow the decisions of the United Nations
India is part of the British Commonwealth so it is not independent
India is neither dependent on any other country nor is it Dominion of any other country
solution: Sovereignty means supreme power. There is no other authority over India. Although India is a member of the Commonwealth, this membership does not affect India's constitutional sovereignty.

question: What is the date of 'Adopted, Enacted and Surrendered' as per the Preamble?
solution: Some provisions, such as the preamble as well as citizenship and elections, were immediately implemented on 26 November 1949. The rest of the Constitution was kept on hold due to the historical significance of 26 January (Purna Swaraj Day).

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with 'The States'?
solution: Part VI is also called the 'Constitution of the States'. Just as Part V works for the Centre, Part VI works for the states.

question: Under which Article 'President's Rule' is imposed under 'Part XVIII' (Emergency)?
solution: Article 356 has been misused the most, hence in the SR Bommai case, the Supreme Court has imposed strict restrictions on its use.

question: What is the 'Official Language of the Union' as per Part XVII (Official Languages) of the Constitution?
solution: Official language means the language used in government work and correspondence. A separate Official Languages ​​Act was enacted to continue the use of English.

question: Which part of the Indian Constitution describes 'Union and its territories'?
solution: Part I defines that India shall be a Union of States. It mentions the names of the states, their boundaries and the power of Parliament to make changes in them.

question: What is true about the legal enforceability of the Preamble?
options: It is enforced by the police
It is enforceable like fundamental rights
It is not enforceable in court
It is enforceable only in the Supreme Court
solution: The Preamble is neither a source of power of the legislature nor places restrictions on its powers. Its main use is as an aid to explain ambiguous provisions of the Constitution.

question: To which articles does Part IX-A (Municipality) of the Constitution extend?
solution: The 74th Amendment promoted decentralization in urban areas. There is a provision for a three-tier system of Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation.

question: In which year did the Supreme Court hold that India is a secular state, before including the word 'secular' in the Preamble?
solution: The 42nd Amendment merely put into words the reality that was already present in various articles of the Constitution. India has been a secular nation since its birth.

question: Who called the Preamble the 'key note' of the Constitution?
solution: Ernest Barker in his book 'Principles of Social and Political Theory' highly praised the Indian Preamble and described it as the master key to understanding the meaning of the entire Constitution.

question: What is the 'philosophical basis' of the introduction?
options: Mixture of liberalism, socialism and humanism
solution: The balance of liberty (liberalism), justice (socialism) and fraternity (humanism) expressed in the Preamble is the real strength of Indian democracy.

question: In which article 'GST Council' is described under 'Part XII'?
solution: The GST Council is headed by the Union Finance Minister. It is a modern example of cooperative federalism where the state and the Center jointly take economic decisions.

question: When was the 'Objective Resolution' accepted by the Constituent Assembly?
solution: The adoption of the Objectives Resolution meant that the Constituent Assembly had decided what the structure and objectives of the future Constitution would be. This became the basis of the introduction.

question: Which approach to 'secularism' has been adopted in India?
solution: Indian secularism is different from western countries. Here the state gives equal protection to all religions. The fundamental rights from Articles 25 to 28 reinforce this sentiment.

question: Which part describes the relations between the Center and the States?
solution: Part XI states on which subjects the Parliament will make laws and on which the State Legislature. Also what will be the procedure in case of dispute.

question: Which articles cannot be suspended when 'Part XVIII' (Emergency) of the Constitution is invoked?
solution: This provision is designed to protect citizens from possible atrocities during an emergency. This was done by learning from the experiences of the Emergency of 1975.

question: What type of socialism has been adopted in the Indian Constitution?
solution: Indian socialism is more inclined towards 'Nehruvian socialism'. It contains a mixture of both Gandhian and Nehruvian elements. Its main objective is to eliminate poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity.

question: Within how much time after declaration of emergency under 'Part XVIII' is the approval of Parliament required?
solution: Emergency can continue further only after it is passed by both houses of Parliament with a special majority. This is a protective shield of parliamentary democracy.

question: According to the Indian form of 'Socialism', what steps does the government take to prevent concentration of wealth?
options: Taking away everyone's property and distributing it equally to everyone is not the way of Indian socialism.
Progressive taxation (higher taxes on the rich) and welfare schemes
Only increasing the salaries of government employees
solution: Schemes like MNREGA, free ration and Ayushman Bharat are attempts to fulfill this 'socialist' goal given in the Preamble.

question: 'Part XIV-A' (Tribunals) was added by which amendment?
solution: Articles 323A and 323B were added under Part XIV-A, aimed at reducing the burden on the judiciary and creating expert bodies for technical matters.

question: To what end does the inclusion of 'social and economic democracy' in the Preamble, in addition to 'democratic' governance, lead?
options: Only increasing military power can be the goal of a dictatorship.
solution: The purpose of the Indian Constitution was not just to create a political structure, but to bring about a social revolution that could end age-old discrimination.

question: Which part of the Constitution deals with 'Amendment'?
solution: Part XX is inspired by the Constitution of South Africa. This shows that the Indian Constitution is neither too rigid nor too flexible, but a mixture of both.

question: What does the word 'democratic' used in the Preamble mean in the context of India?
solution: In Indian democracy, Parliament is accountable to the executive. It is also called the 'Westminster Model' or Responsive Governance.

question: How many articles are given for Panchayats in 'Part IX'?
solution: Along with giving constitutional status to Panchayats, 11th Schedule was also added to the Constitution, in which 29 business subjects are given.

question: Who appoints the 'Advocate General' under 'Part VI' (States)?
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
solution: The Advocate General is the first law officer of the state government. He can participate in the proceedings of the State Assembly but cannot vote there.

question: Which Schedule was added for 'Municipalities' under Part IX-A?
solution: Municipalities are constituted at three levels – Nagar Panchayat (transitional areas), Municipal Council (smaller cities) and Municipal Corporation (larger cities).

question: Who called the Preamble the 'most precious part' of the Constitution and the 'jewel of the Constitution'?
solution: Thakur Das Bhargava described the Preamble as the soul of the Constitution and a yardstick by which the value of the entire Constitution can be measured.

question: Which part of the Constitution was removed by the '7th Constitutional Amendment Act 1956'?
options: The old category of was abolished and Part VII was repealed. B) Part IX
solution: In the original Constitution, the states were divided into four categories. After the reorganization of states on the basis of language in 1956, these categories were abolished and Part VII became irrelevant.

question: Who constitutes the 'Inter-State Council' under 'Part XI'?
solution: This council is a forum to examine disputes between states and discuss matters of common interest. It was first formed in 1990 on the recommendation of a government commission.

question: In which Article the High Court has the power to issue writs under 'Part VI'?
solution: Article 226 is a very important constitutional weapon which protects the citizens against the arbitrariness of the administration.

question: How many types of amendment procedures are mentioned in Article 368 under 'Part XX'?
options: Such a big Constitution cannot be changed by just one process.
solution: Article 368 does not give unlimited power to the Parliament. It cannot amend the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

question: 'Part V' (The Union) extends to which articles?
solution: Part V defines the functioning of the executive, legislature and judiciary of the Union. The complete structure of the central government is given in it.

question: Why is India called a 'Republic'?
options: Because here the Prime Minister is the most powerful
Because here the head of the state (President) is elected and not hereditary
Because here the Constitution is supreme
solution: America and India are republics because here the President is elected. In contrast, Britain is not a republic because the post of Queen or King is hereditary.

question: In which part of the Constitution has the provision of Panchayats been added?
solution: Articles 243 to 243-O under Part IX mention the composition, reservation and powers of Panchayats. It strengthens rural local self-governance.

question: For whom is the provision of 'Citizenship by Descent' under 'Part II' (Citizenship)?
options: Those who are foreign refugees have to register or acquire citizenship by naturalization.
Those who are born outside India but whose parents are Indians
Those who are born only in India
solution: This provision is important for those Indians who live abroad for job or studies and their children are born there.

question: According to 'Part XVII', in which article is the provision of 'education in mother tongue at primary level'?
solution: Its objective is to preserve regional languages ​​and make education easier for children. It was added by the 7th Amendment.

question: Who appoints the members of the Public Service Commission under 'Part XIV'?
options: President for the Union and Governor for the States
The Chairman of UPSC himself is also appointed by the President.
solution: Part XIV ensures that the selection of public servants is free from political influence. Once appointed, their removal is also subject to a complex constitutional process (Article 317).

question: What is the correct sequence of the ideals of 'justice' in the Preamble?
solution: Social justice means that no one in the society should be discriminated against on the basis of caste or religion. Economic justice means equitable distribution of resources. Political justice means equal participation of all in governance.

question: The inspiration for the word 'socialism' in the preamble has been taken from the revolution of which country?
solution: The Russian Revolution of 1917 spread the idea of ​​social equality and equal distribution of wealth throughout the world. The makers of the Indian Constitution were influenced by this and included three forms of justice in the Preamble.

question: Who is exempted from legal proceedings under Article 361 of 'Part XIX'?
solution: This exemption has been given so that the people holding the highest constitutional posts of the country can perform their duties without any fear or legal hindrance. After leaving office, cases can be filed against him.

question: Who described the Preamble as the 'political horoscope' of the Constitution?
solution: Political horoscope means that the Preamble defines the political direction of future India and its goals. Munshi ji believed that this reveals the destiny of the Constitution.

question: 'Part IX-B' (Cooperative Societies) is linked with which fundamental right?
solution: The 97th Amendment not only gave a new Part (IX-B) to cooperative societies but also made it a fundamental right of the citizens so that economic democracy at the grassroots level was strengthened.

question: For which state there are no special provisions under Article 371 in 'Part XXI' of the Indian Constitution?
solution: Part XXI was not exclusive to Jammu and Kashmir. It has several sub-paragraphs 'A' to 'J' which give special status to states like North-Eastern States, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Goa due to their specific circumstances.

question: What is the tenure of Panchayats under 'Part IX'?
options: 5 years from the date of election
solution: It is now the constitutional obligation of the state government to conduct Panchayat elections on time. If the Panchayat is dissolved prematurely, the new Panchayat will function only for the remaining term.

question: To which ideology does the use of the word 'socialist' in the preamble indicate?
options: Mixed form of Marxism and Gandhism
solution: The Supreme Court has also clarified that the objective of Indian socialism is to protect the citizen 'from the cradle to the grave' and to reduce economic inequality.

question: In which part of the Constitution is the provision for tribunals?
solution: To reduce the burden on courts, tribunals are established for speedy resolution of administrative and other disputes. CAT is an example of this.

question: Under which Article the Governor is appointed under 'Part VI' (States)?
solution: Part VI defines the systems of governance of the states. In this, complete information is given about the Chief Minister, Governor, Legislative Assembly and High Court (Article 214).

question: According to the word 'Republic' used in the Preamble, in whom is the supreme power vested in India?
options: This oligarchy occurs only among rich businessmen.
Among the representatives elected by the public
solution: India is a 'democratic republic'. This means that political sovereignty rests with the citizens rather than in the hands of any one person (such as the king).

question: Which word in the Indian Constitution is considered more appropriate for the word 'secular'?
solution: Secularism means that the state will not have any declared religion of its own and will treat all sects equally. This reflects India's tradition of 'Equality of all religions'.

question: 'Sovereignty' also means that India:
options: Will act only on the orders of the United Nations
Cannot give away any part of its land
Will always be in a state of war
solution: The merger of Sikkim with India (1975) is an example of this sovereign power of India. India included it in its union as a sovereign nation.

question: 'Part II' of the Indian Constitution deals with which subject?
solution: There is a provision for single citizenship in India. Who will be a citizen at the time the Constitution comes into force is explained in Part II, while the Citizenship Act 1955 was created for the latter.

question: From which revolution are the ideals of 'liberty, equality and fraternity' taken in the Preamble?
solution: The French Revolution gave the principle of 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity'. The makers of the Indian Constitution aimed to bring about deep changes in the Indian society by including it in the Preamble.

question: What opinion did the Supreme Court give regarding the Preamble in the Berubari Union case (1960)?
options: The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution
The preamble is the most powerful part
The Preamble is not a part of the Constitution
solution: In the Berubari case, the court accepted the importance of the Preamble but refused to consider it technically a part of the Constitution. This decision was changed after 13 years.

question: When were the words 'unity of the nation' changed to 'unity and integrity of the nation' in the Preamble?
solution: The term 'integrity' ensures that no part of India can demand separation from the country and the geographical boundaries of the country will remain intact.

question: The words 'We the people of India' used in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of which country?
solution: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution begins with the words 'We the people of India'. This is similar to the US Constitution which begins with 'We the People'. This phrase makes it clear that in India the people are supreme and the Constitution derives its power from the people only. It has been given neither by any king nor by any external power.

question: 'Part XIV' deals with which important subject?
options: Services under the Union and the States (UPSC and State PSCs)
solution: Part XIV ensures that there is an independent and impartial merit-based bureaucracy to run the administration of the country. UPSC is formed under Article 315.

question: Which important institution is described in Article 280 of 'Part XII'?
solution: The Finance Commission is appointed by the President every five years. This is an important pillar to strengthen Cooperative Federalism.

question: In which article 'Pardon Power' has been given to the President under 'Part V'?
solution: This power of the President is not judicial but executive. Its purpose is to correct a judicial mistake or to grant mercy on humanitarian grounds.

question: With which important document did Justice Mohammad Hidayatullah compare the Preamble?
solution: Former Chief Justice Mohammad Hidayatullah had said that the Preamble is the soul of our Constitution and is reminiscent of the United States Declaration of Independence, but it is more than just a declaration.

question: What is the meaning of the word 'liberty' in the Preamble?
options: Absence of unreasonable restrictions on activities and opportunities for development of personality
solution: The Preamble and the Fundamental Rights together ensure that the State does not interfere with the personal liberty of an individual without any valid reason.

question: Emergency Provisions are mentioned in which part?
solution: There are three types of emergency in India: Articles 352 (national), 356 (failure of constitutional machinery in the states) and 360 (financial). This part is influenced by the Constitution of Germany.

question: In which Article the date of commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950) is mentioned under 'Part XXII'?
solution: Part XXII is the last part of the Constitution which deals with the technical formalities. The reason for choosing 26 January as Republic Day was the Lahore session of 1930.

question: In which part and article the process of amendment of the Constitution is given?
solution: Article 368 provides for two methods of amendment: special majority and support of half the states with special majority. However, Parliament cannot change the basic structure.

question: Can the 'Preamble' be amended under Article 368 of 'Part XX' of the Constitution?
options: Yes, provided it is not against the basic structure
solution: The Preamble has been amended once (42nd Amendment). This proved that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution and can be changed as per the needs of the times, provided its core values ​​are not disturbed.

question: Who constitutes the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language under 'Part XVII'?
solution: The function of this committee is to see what progress has been made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and to make recommendations to the President in this regard.
